author: 0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~B
subject: P4(comp-surface-check): TOOL=WORKS, GATE=CANNOT-BLOCK-BY-CONSTRUCTION. First three-rail negative-control fixture in NFRA_TOOLCHECK. R1: a SEV1 surface member (portal/src/pages/ModelPortfolios.tsx, alarms via model_portfolios.headline AND .benchmark -- the sharpest input, not the most obvious) MUST rc=2 + CRITICAL. R3: a benign path stays rc=0 + OK. R2 VARIANCE: the recorder emits BOTH, so R1's red is evidence. Killed by 3 mutants (aim R1 at benign -> R1 fails; make the two controls identical -> R2 fails as UNDISCRIMINATING; trap test survives a mode flip). THE GATE IS THE FINDING: safe-commit.sh:417-418 runs it --mode advisory (computes CRITICAL, returns 0), PIPES to sed (rc becomes sed's), and appends || true -- THREE independent exit-code maskings -- and never branches on the verdict at all: no if, no rc capture, no exit. Positive control: 'set -o pipefail' restores rc=2, proving the verdict existed and the WIRING discards it. THE TRAP the fixture guards: flipping advisory->blocking changes NOTHING (masks 2+3 remain) while the CRITICAL line still prints, so the obvious repair looks successful and is not. DECLARATIVE drift: the tool's own header says 'SEV1=block-with-ack' and CLAUDE.md calls it a GATE / 'SEV1 = must-always-be-right', while safe-commit.sh:409 says 'QUERY-only; never blocks' -- three records, two stories. Method note, banked: my FIRST R1 run PASSED 'assert rc != 0' on a tool that never executed -- subprocess(['bash',...]) on Windows resolves WSL's bash (execvpe /bin/bash, rc=1) while shutil.which returns Git Bash. A broken interpreter is also non-zero. That is comp-tagauthz's defect (P4 s6) reproduced inside the fixture written to catch it, and only 'rc==2 AND CRITICAL AND the surface name' caught it. So the fixture now positive-controls its own interpreter (exit 7) and NEVER resolves bash by name. A negative control must assert the SPECIFIC red, never merely non-zero.

So a malformed invocation returns the tool's RED on ANY input, benign or not -- CTO got rc=2 on both paths and only his positive control caught it. Therefore 'assert rc == 2' is NOT the specific red either; it is UNDISCRIMINATING between a verdict and a typo. author: 0.4.0_DS_ClientPlatform~B
subject: P4(comp-freshness partition-key): RE-VERDICT ANTI-CORRELATED, per TO s5's order to re-examine every seed against the sharper class. The seed is wrong in BOTH directions. (a) It does NOT parse the filename: _DATE_KEY_RE.search(line) takes the FIRST YYYY-MM-DD on an 'aws s3 ls' line, and such a line BEGINS with LastModified -- '2026-07-09 21:38:12  1234 2026-07-01.parquet' returns 2026-07-09. Its own docstring promises 'the MAX YYYY-MM-DD parsed from the object FILENAMES (the stamped as_of date-key)' and 'the basis is the DATE-KEY, NEVER MTIME'. IT READS MTIME -- the one thing it swears it never reads. (b) 'reads no row, in any mode' is FALSE: content-mode json-loads the doc and resolves as_of_field. The seed accused it of the lesser crime. WHY ANTI-CORRELATED not UNDISCRIMINATING: healthy artifact (key==mtime) CORRECT; plain-stale never-rewritten CORRECT; the FROZEN as_of REWRITTEN DAILY -- the exact failure this mode was implemented to catch -- WRONG and reads GREEN, because the daily rewrite that IS the freeze drags LastModified forward. It PASSES an arbitrary-input control and reports GREEN precisely where the fault lives. The two dates coincide exactly when the pipeline is healthy and diverge exactly when it is broken, and the tool reads the wrong one. AND THE FREEZE DETECTOR IS DEAD CODE: comp-freshness:698 guards on status(stamped_age) in (FAIL,WARN) AND mtime_status(age_h)==PASS, printing MTIME-FRESH-BUT-PARTITION-STALE (stamped-as_of freeze) -- but both operands derive from the SAME max-LastModified, one merely truncated to midnight. Their difference is always in [0,24), a pure truncation artifact a real freeze does not move. The guard can fire ONLY when truncation straddles a threshold (on a HEALTHY artifact) and can NEVER fire on the freeze it names: a correctly-designed detector whose two inputs are one measurement. R5: _aws(check_aws=False) returns None on credentials/403/timeout, mapped to the same None as an empty prefix, and the consumer prints 'PARTITION-KEY UNCHECKED (no date-key object under prefix)' -- ONE CAUSE NAMED FOR TWO CONDITIONS; a denied read is reported as an absent object. LIVE SCOPE: 5 entries (yaml.safe_load; grep -c says 6 and the sixth is a comment -- the mention-vs-registration error COO made at 033832Z and I then repeated), all cot silver {holdings,unrealized,allocations,transactions,realized}, two at severity=ERROR. cot is a separate firm, in scope; NO bd/49F/Schwab prefix touched. Fixture contacts NO AWS (_aws monkeypatched with recorded ls line shapes). 8/8, commit-gate rc=0, 2 killing mutants -- M1 simulates the real fix (parse the key) and exactly the 4 defect-asserting tests go RED while all 4 positive controls stay GREEN, which is the invert-on-fix contract.
